name: exp3-iter4-critique-stats
description: exp3 iter_4 PPC stats on forward_continuation_response_bias; order-split forward lean -0.11, even-set gap 0.38, next-term +0.12
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-31, exp3 iter_4 critique of forward_continuation_response_bias. iter_3's 8 stats were all null. Observed values: forward lean on ascending-shown sets minus descending-shown sets is -0.108, so the lean is stronger when the examples were shown descending. The design has 41 ascending and 39 descending sets. Above-max targets 1-10 above minus more than 20 above is +0.057. Arithmetic next term (last + step) minus other targets is +0.123. Digit reversal is -0.066. Double or half of an example is +0.10. All-even sets, even minus odd targets, is 0.376. Span centre minus edges is 0.003. Same-set lag-1 response agreement is 0.617.
**Why:** these are candidate discrepancies; iter_4/critique/ppc_results.json says which are significant.
**How to apply:** if the order split is significant, make the forward lean depend on the order the examples were shown in. Related: [[exp3-iter3-critique-stats]], [[forward-continuation-response-bias]].
---
name: forward-continuation-response-bias
description: exp3 iter3 decision-stage screens on round_landmark_veto — signed above/below logit tilt +3.7 loglik; gain/criterion/any-k/all-k and format veto null
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-31, exp3 iter_3/candidate_2, MAP screens on round_landmark_veto (base MAP loglik -3415.3):
- Signed logit tilt, +1 if target is above the largest example and -1 if below the smallest: -3411.6 (tilt 0.14). A two-sided version gives up≈down≈0.14, so the effect is symmetric. Submitted as `forward_continuation_response_bias`.
- Null (within 0.2): logit gain+criterion (gain 1.03), 1-(1-p)^k, p^k, and a numeral-format veto (single digit / round / other). The single-digit part fits to 0, and adding it makes the round veto worse (-3418.7).
- The base is well calibrated by predicted bin and on examples-as-targets (obs 0.757 vs pred 0.791). Raw residuals: above obs 0.387 vs pred 0.369; below 0.258 vs 0.278.

**Why:** on exp3 the decision stage is probability matching. Only the above/below direction leaves a residual.
**How to apply:** scripts are in iter_3/candidate_2/scratch (map.py, dump.py, dir_*.py). See [[exp3-decision-stage-screens]], [[forward-counting-tilt-finding]].
---
name: exp3-iter1-exploratory-screens
description: exp3 iter1 cand1 MAP screens on the fives incumbent (loglik -3436.7); weak-sampling ranges, rote tables, production readout, noise all null or worse; hard 7/8 tables +2.2
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-31, exp3 iter_1/candidate_1 (`hard_seven_eight_tables`). Base: fives_privileged_decoupled_prime_odd, MAP loglik -3436.7.
- Range sampling exponent (0 = weak, 1 = strong): fits 0.84, +0.4. Null.
- Rote times tables (m×1..10 or ×12): -340 to -450. People extend 4s, 6s and 3s beyond 10m.
- Posterior-predictive "production" readout (size-weighted, then a logistic): -124.
- Fixed NOISE 0.03 or 0.2: worse by 7 and 15. 0.1 is about optimal.
- Extra cost on multiples of 7 and 8 (rows 20, 21): +2.2, cost 0.65, RMSE vs base 0.012. This one was submitted; the check printed OK, smoke loglik -3442.0, 116 s for the smoke chain.
The worst-fit sets (excess nll over a saturated model): 3,33,99 (39); 8,64 (29: multiples of 8 predicted 0.7, observed 0.3); 83,38,58,68 (26: 85/87/89 observed 0.9, predicted 0.4); 14,98,91 (15: multiples of 7 predicted 0.7, observed 0.2). Aggregate calibration is fine.
Screen script: iter_1/candidate_1/scratch/rote2.py <mode> <K> <model.py>. Get p_yes with m.replace_rvs_by_values; m.compile_fn evaluates at random RV draws.

**Why:** the response stage, the sampling assumption and the noise rate are all exhausted on exp3.
**How to apply:** the remaining residuals are idiosyncratic per set. Related: [[concept-space-saturated-exp3]], [[exp3-decision-stage-screens]].
---
name: exp3-decision-stage-screens
description: exp3 decision-rule screens on repdigit incumbent — all near null; singleton-only guessing +2.4 loglik best
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-31, exp3 iter_0/candidate_0 (`single_example_guessing`). find_MAP on repdigit_pattern_chart_concepts (base loglik -3465.9, the incumbent's lapse goes to 0). Results:
- uncertainty-gated guessing (both the 0.5 and the fitted-guess versions): giveup goes to 0, gain 0.0. This was +23 in exp2 ([[uncertainty-triggered-guessing]]) but does not replicate.
- logit yes-bias: +0.4. Gain plus bias: +0.7 (gain 1.04).
- separate coin-flip guess share for single-example sets: +2.4 (share 0.15). This one was submitted; its smoke loglik was -3470.3 and the smoke fit took 95 s.
The machine has 1 CPU, so each MAP screen takes ~3-4 min.

**Why:** on exp3 the residuals are not in the response stage.
**How to apply:** look for exp3 gains in the concepts and the prior, not in the lapse or bias form.

name: fitted-stray-rate-on-veto-exp3
description: exp3 iter3 cand4 repair — free stray rate on round_landmark_veto +3.8 MAP (0.069 vs fixed 0.1); 7 other one-param screens ≤2.5
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-31, exp3 iter_3/candidate_4_repair_1 (`trusted_example_round_landmark_veto`). The first attempt (veto + spacing) was rejected as a duplicate of round_veto_spacing_sparsity.
- On the incumbent (MAP -3415.3), a free stray rate with prior Beta(2,18) gives -3411.5, with the rate at 0.069. This was submitted. Check OK, smoke -3419.7, 140 s.
- Gains of the other screens:
  - interval Erlang shape exponent +2.5
  - hard 7/8 tables +2.0
  - target-1 endpoint veto +0.6
  - singleton guessing +0.2
  - log nearest-distance logit shift +0.1
  - repeat aversion for targets that are examples 0
- Gotcha: the incumbent's rule rows are 16=mult 3 … 20=mult 7, 21=mult 8.
**Why:** stray rate had been null in exp1, but it revives on the current base.
**How to apply:** scripts are in iter_3/candidate_4_repair_1/scratch (var.py A/B/D/R flags, var2.py E/H/J flags). Related: [[veto-plus-spacing-exp3]], [[spacing-plus-round-veto-exp3]].

"""Forward-continuation response bias on the round-landmark-veto learner.

At the answer stage people treat the examples as what the program has produced
so far, and they assume it runs upward. So, beyond what the inferred concept
implies, they lean toward yes for a target above the largest example and
toward no for a target below the smallest. One fitted, signed shift on the
log-odds of saying yes sets the strength of this lean; targets inside the
examples' span are unaffected. Concept inference is round_landmark_veto's,
unchanged: primitive-built rules with costs, final-digit discount, power and
square costs, graded times tables, prime bonus and odd cost, repdigits,
privileged fives, hundred-chart ranges, the size principle, set-size-graded
evidence weight, near-all-or-none commitment and the veto of round targets
that no round example supports.
"""
import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

N = 100
NUMS = np.arange(1, N + 1)


def _rules():
    r, c = [NUMS % 2 == 1, NUMS % 2 == 0], [1, 1]
    primes = np.array([n > 1 and all(n % d for d in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1)) for n in NUMS])
    r.append(primes)
    r.append(np.isin(NUMS, [k * k for k in range(1, 11)]))
    r.append(np.isin(NUMS, [k ** 3 for k in range(1, 5)]))
    c += [2, 2, 2]
    for b in range(2, 11):
        r.append(np.isin(NUMS, [b ** k for k in range(0, 8) if b ** k <= N]))
        c.append(2)
    p2 = [2 ** k for k in range(0, 7)]
    r.append(np.isin(NUMS, [x for x in p2 if x != 32]))
    r.append(np.isin(NUMS, p2 + [37]))
    c += [3, 3]
    for m in list(range(3, 10)) + [11, 12]:
        r.append(NUMS % m == 0)
        c.append(2)
    n_before = len(r)
    for d in range(10):
        r.append(NUMS % 10 == d)
        c.append(2)
    ends = np.zeros(len(r) + 10)
    ends[n_before:len(r)] = 1.0
    for d in range(10):
        r.append(np.array([str(d) in str(n) for n in NUMS]))
        c.append(2)
    exp_ = np.zeros(len(r))
    exp_[4:16] = 1.0  # cubes, powers of 2-10, two powers-of-2 variants
    sq = np.zeros(len(r))
    sq[3] = 1.0  # perfect squares
    log_m = np.zeros(len(r))
    log_m[18:27] = np.log(np.array(list(range(3, 10)) + [11, 12]) / 3.0)  # as in the incumbent
    pr = np.zeros(len(r))
    pr[2] = 1.0  # prime numbers: their own bonus
    od = np.zeros(len(r))
    od[0] = 1.0  # odd numbers: their own cost
    fv = np.zeros(len(r))
    fv[18] = 1.0  # multiples of 5: their own bonus
    r.append(np.isin(NUMS, [11 * k for k in range(1, 10)]))  # repdigits
    c.append(2)
    ends, exp_, sq, log_m, pr, od, fv = (np.append(a, 0.0) for a in (ends, exp_, sq, log_m, pr, od, fv))
    rep = np.zeros(len(r))
    rep[-1] = 1.0
    return np.array(r, dtype=float), np.array(c, dtype=float), ends, exp_, sq, log_m, pr, od, rep, fv


RULES, RULE_COST, IS_END, IS_EXP, IS_SQ, LOG_FACTOR, IS_PRIME, IS_ODD, IS_REP, IS_FIVES = _rules()
assert RULES[18, 4] == 1 and RULES[18].sum() == 20  # row 18 is multiples of 5
N_RULES = RULES.shape[0]
RULE_SIZES = RULES.sum(1)
NOISE = 0.1
MAX_N = 4

# Interval groups: (size, whole-rows flag, number of examples contained).
_iv = [(a, b) for a in range(1, N + 1) for b in range(a, N + 1)]
IV_A = np.array([a for a, _ in _iv])
IV_B = np.array([b for _, b in _iv])
IV_SIZE = IV_B - IV_A + 1
IV_ROW = ((IV_A % 10 == 1) & (IV_B % 10 == 0)).astype(int)
SR_KEY = (IV_SIZE - 1) * 2 + IV_ROW  # 0..199
SR_COUNT = np.bincount(SR_KEY, minlength=200).astype(float)
SR_SIZE = np.repeat(np.arange(1, N + 1), 2).astype(float)
SR_ROW = np.tile([0.0, 1.0], N)
SR_LOGCOUNT = np.where(SR_COUNT > 0, np.log(np.maximum(SR_COUNT, 1.0)), -1e10)
G = 200 * (MAX_N + 1)
G_SIZE = np.repeat(SR_SIZE, MAX_N + 1)
G_ROW = np.repeat(SR_ROW, MAX_N + 1)
G_C = np.tile(np.arange(MAX_N + 1), 200).astype(float)
G_SR = np.repeat(np.arange(200), MAX_N + 1)


def prepare_observed(rows):
    sets, idx, set_i, tgt = [], {}, [], []
    for r in rows:
        s = str(r["number_set"]).strip()
        if s not in idx:
            idx[s] = len(sets)
            sets.append([int(x) for x in s.split(",")])
        set_i.append(idx[s])
        tgt.append(int(float(r["target"])))
    S = len(sets)
    rule_ll = np.zeros((S, N_RULES))
    n_ex = np.zeros(S)
    cnt_set = np.zeros((S, G))
    iv_c = []
    for i, ex in enumerate(sets):
        for x in ex:
            pin = RULES[:, x - 1] * (1 - NOISE) / RULE_SIZES
            rule_ll[i] += np.log(pin + NOISE / N)
        n_ex[i] = len(ex)
        c = sum(((IV_A <= x) & (IV_B >= x)).astype(int) for x in ex)
        iv_c.append(c)
        cnt_set[i] = np.bincount(SR_KEY * (MAX_N + 1) + c, minlength=G)
    pair_idx, pairs, pidx = [], [], {}
    for s, t in zip(set_i, tgt):
        if (s, t) not in pidx:
            pidx[(s, t)] = len(pairs)
            pairs.append((s, t))
        pair_idx.append(pidx[(s, t)])
    cnt_pair = np.zeros((len(pairs), G))
    for j, (s, t) in enumerate(pairs):
        inside = (IV_A <= t) & (IV_B >= t)
        cnt_pair[j] = np.bincount(SR_KEY[inside] * (MAX_N + 1) + iv_c[s][inside], minlength=G)
    pair_set = np.array([s for s, _ in pairs], dtype="int64")
    pair_tgt = np.array([t for _, t in pairs])
    # Round target that no example supports (no example is a multiple of 10).
    unsupported_round = np.array([float(t % 10 == 0 and not any(e % 10 == 0 for e in sets[s])) for s, t in pairs])
    # +1 target above every example, -1 below every example, 0 inside the span.
    direction = np.array([float(t > max(sets[s])) - float(t < min(sets[s])) for s, t in pairs])
    set_mask = np.where(cnt_set > 0, 0.0, -1e10)
    return {
        "rule_loglik": rule_ll,
        "n_examples": n_ex,
        "group_count_set": cnt_set,
        "group_mask_set": set_mask,
        "group_count_pair": cnt_pair,
        "rule_member_pair": RULES[:, pair_tgt - 1].T.copy(),
        "pair_set": pair_set,
        "unsupported_round_pair": unsupported_round,
        "direction_pair": direction,
        "pair_idx": np.array(pair_idx, dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(float(r["rating"])) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }


with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_loglik = pm.Data("rule_loglik", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))
    n_examples = pm.Data("n_examples", np.ones(1))
    group_count_set = pm.Data("group_count_set", np.zeros((1, G)))
    group_mask_set = pm.Data("group_mask_set", np.zeros((1, G)))
    group_count_pair = pm.Data("group_count_pair", np.zeros((1, G)))
    rule_member_pair = pm.Data("rule_member_pair", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))
    pair_set = pm.Data("pair_set", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    unsupported_round_pair = pm.Data("unsupported_round_pair", np.zeros(1))
    direction_pair = pm.Data("direction_pair", np.zeros(1))
    pair_idx = pm.Data("pair_idx", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lam = pm.Beta("lambda_rules", 2.0, 2.0)  # prior mass on rules vs intervals
    cost = pm.HalfNormal("primitive_cost", sigma=5.0)  # log-prior cost per extra primitive
    log_beta = pm.Normal("log_beta", 0.5, 1.0)  # commitment exponent (log scale)
    beta = pm.Deterministic("beta", pt.exp(log_beta))
    lapse = pm.Beta("lapse", 1.0, 10.0)
    end_bonus = pm.Normal("final_digit_bonus", 0.0, 2.0)
    exp_cost = pm.Normal("exponent_cost", 0.0, 3.0)
    sq_cost = pm.Normal("square_cost", 0.0, 3.0)
    mult_cost = pm.Normal("mult_cost", 0.0, 3.0)
    row_bonus = pm.Normal("row_bonus", 0.0, 5.0)
    prime_bonus = pm.Normal("prime_bonus", 0.0, 3.0)  # prime bonus and odd cost are separate
    odd_cost = pm.Normal("odd_cost", 0.0, 3.0)
    rep_bonus = pm.Normal("repdigit_bonus", 0.0, 2.0)
    fives_bonus = pm.Normal("fives_bonus", 0.0, 2.0)  # multiples of 5 privileged
    # Per-example evidence weight grows with set size (centred at 3 examples).
    evidence_growth = pm.Normal("evidence_growth", 0.0, 1.0)
    ev_w = pt.exp(evidence_growth * pt.log(n_examples / 3.0))
    # The one change: share of unsupported round targets vetoed as non-outputs.
    round_veto = pm.Beta("round_veto", 1.0, 4.0)
    log_sigma = pm.Normal("log_sigma", np.log(20.0), 1.0)

    log_sigma = pm.Normal("log_sigma", np.log(20.0), 1.0)
    sigma = pm.Deterministic("sigma", pt.exp(log_sigma))

    # prefers diagnostic numbers, so a concept's effective size is the sum of its
    # members' distinctiveness raised to this power (0 = random sampling).

"""Single source of truth for MCMC sampler settings.

Every entry point (outer-loop run CLI, inner-loop run CLI, the PPC critique
CLI, design-time family-twin fits) reads its defaults from here, so "what
settings did this run use?" has one answer unless a config overrides it
explicitly.
"""

# Production sampling: full posteriors for model comparison (ELPD-LOO needs
# reliable log-likelihood draws). Quick local runs should pass explicit lower
# values rather than lowering these. A model whose posterior geometry makes
# 0.99 needlessly expensive can declare its own SAMPLER_SETTINGS in its file.
PRODUCTION_DRAWS = 4000
PRODUCTION_TUNE = 3000
PRODUCTION_CHAINS = 4
PRODUCTION_TARGET_ACCEPT = 0.99

# Chains run in parallel, one worker process each. Matches PRODUCTION_CHAINS
# so every chain gets its own core. Callers that fit many models concurrently
# should pass cores=1 explicitly to avoid oversubscribing the machine.
PRODUCTION_CORES = 4

# Design-time fits: the settings the posterior-informed design refitted every
# carried model at until 2026-10-08, when it began loading the previous model
# loop's own fits instead (user decision). Kept only to rebuild designs made
# with them (scripts/subjective_randomness/validate_lazy_eig.py).
DESIGN_TWIN_DRAWS = 500
DESIGN_TWIN_TUNE = 500
DESIGN_TWIN_CHAINS = 2
# Those fits used a model's own SAMPLER_SETTINGS target_accept when it
# declared one, else this: a compromise between the production 0.99 (slow,
# tiny steps) and PyMC's 0.8 (user decision, 2026-09-26).
DESIGN_TWIN_TARGET_ACCEPT = 0.9

# Convergence gate (admission, export, pruning): a fit is converged when at
# most MAX_DIVERGENCE_FRACTION of its transitions diverged and R-hat <= MAX_R_HAT
# and bulk ESS >= MIN_BULK_ESS on every free parameter (user decision
# 2026-09-26: the strict gate of Vehtari et al. (2021) — R-hat 1.01, ESS 400, no
# divergences — rejected most seed models).
MAX_R_HAT = 1.05
